create.name: Buddha at the Gas Pump
create.bio:
Buddha at the Gas Pump, usually shortened to BatGap, is a long-form interview show about spiritual awakening, hosted by Rick Archer and run with his wife Irene as a small non-profit from rural Iowa. Both spent many years as meditation teachers and on extended meditation courses before the show began in 2009. The early episodes were filmed with local guests in person; from 2010 the conversations moved online, so guests could join from anywhere in the world, and the YouTube channel has been running since late 2009.

Each episode is a relaxed one-to-two-hour conversation with someone who describes a shift in their sense of self: teachers and practitioners from Buddhist, Hindu, Christian, tantric and non-dual backgrounds, alongside people with no tradition at all. Rick asks how the change came about, how they practise and what everyday life is like afterwards. More than 760 interviews are archived on the website with indexes by name, year and category, transcripts and a full-text search, and the show is also released as an audio podcast. The site notes that featuring a guest is not an endorsement.

free_resources.title: BatGap audio podcast
free_resources.description: Every interview is also published as an audio podcast; this page lists the apps and feeds where it can be followed for free.
